judge_response:
ANALYSIS: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) and IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis (IgG4-SC) are distinct biliary disorders with different pathophysiologies, demographics, imaging features, serologic profiles, and treatment responses. PSC is a chronic, progressive, immune-mediated fibroinflammatory disease of intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts, strongly associated with IBD (especially ulcerative colitis), typically showing multifocal strictures with beading on MRCP/ERCP, and normal or only mildly elevated IgG4. IgG4-SC is part of the systemic IgG4-related disease spectrum, often presenting with dominant strictures (especially in the proximal common bile duct), elevated serum IgG4, characteristic histology (lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis), and dramatic response to corticosteroids. While they can mimic each other radiologically, they are *not interchangeable diagnoses* — misclassifying PSC as IgG4-SC may lead to inappropriate steroid therapy and delayed surveillance for cholangiocarcinoma (a known complication of PSC).

VERDICT: INCORRECT
